hints: Every one of the n positions independently has two choices: 0 or 1.
Multiply the number of choices per position rather than listing bit strings.
The result grows quickly, so reduce modulo 1,000,000,007.
analogy: Each bit position is a separate two-choice switch.
example: For n=3, the choices are 2*2*2=8 bit strings.
correctness: Independent choices multiply, yielding exactly 2^n strings; modular reduction preserves the requested remainder.
complexity: O(log n) time with repeated squaring, or O(n) with repeated multiplication; O(1) extra space.
algorithm: Compute 2^n modulo 1,000,000,007 by repeated squaring, or multiply by 2 n times while reducing modulo the modulus.
